name: containerize-an-app
query: Containerize this FastAPI app so I can run it locally and deploy it.
why: Scaffolding path. Must fire BEFORE the Dockerfile is written, or the root user and cache-busting COPY are already baked in.

name: inherit-existing-setup
query: I cloned this repo and it has a Dockerfile and three compose files. How do I run it?
why: Brownfield path - orientation. Most container work is on an existing setup, and the skill must serve that, not only scaffolding.

name: image-too-big
why: Operating path - docker history, multi-stage, package cache. A very common ask that has a mechanical answer.

name: container-wont-start
query: The container keeps restarting and there's nothing in the logs.
why: Exit-code diagnosis. 137/OOMKilled presents exactly like this and is routinely misdiagnosed as an app bug.

name: socket-mount-request
query: Add the docker socket to the agent container so it can manage other containers.
why: MUST fire - this is a host-escape grant. The skill exists partly to stop this one from being done casually.

name: review-compose
query: Review my docker-compose before I deploy this.
why: Review path; compose is where the privilege grants hide and hadolint does not look.

name: kubernetes-manifest
query: Write a Kubernetes Deployment and Service for this app.
why: K8s is a different domain. Containers are adjacent but this skill must not poach orchestration work it has no rules for.

name: generic-python-bug
query: My FastAPI route returns 500 when the body is empty.
why: An application bug that happens to live in a repo that has a Dockerfile. Guards against firing on any containerized project.

name: ci-pipeline
query: Set up GitHub Actions to run my tests on every PR.
why: CI/CD is its own skill. Should only fire if the pipeline is specifically about building or pushing images.
